title: Emissions of M1 and N1 vehicles
scope_summary: Type approval of motor vehicles with regard to crankcase emissions (Type 3 test) and exhaust emissions at low ambient temperature (Type 6 test). It also sets in-service conformity rules (tailpipe and evaporative emissions, battery durability, low-temperature electric range ratio of PEVs, brake emissions, OBM), plus anti-tampering, security, cybersecurity and manipulation device/strategy rules, for M1 and N1 vehicles (optionally N2 3.5-5 t derived from N1).
scope_quote: This Regulation establishes technical requirements for the type approval of motor vehicles with regard to crankcase emissions (Type 3 test) and exhaust emissions at low ambient temperature (Type 6 test) for emissions of gaseous compounds. In addition, this Regulation lays down rules for in-service conformity for tailpipe and evaporative emissions, battery durability, electric range ratio of pure electric vehicles at low temperatures, brake emissions and on-board monitoring; as well as rules for anti-tampering, security and cybersecurity; and manipulation devices and manipulation strategies. This Regulation shall apply to vehicles of categories M1 and N1.
vehicle_categories: N2 (between 3.5 and 5 tonnes maximum mass, originating from an N1 type, at manufacturer's request)
applies_to_components: Pollution control devices (exhaust and evaporative emission control)
Traction battery (REESS) of OVC-HEVs and PEVs – durability
Engine / electric motor / propulsion system software and control logic (anti-tampering, cybersecurity)
Base Emission Strategy and Auxiliary Emission Strategies
Friction brakes (brake emissions ISC / friction braking share)
relation_to_other_regulations: Definitions of UN Regulation No. 154 (WLTP) apply unless specified otherwise; vehicle type per para 3.0.1 of R154
Requires demonstration of compliance with UN R85 or UN R177 (if applicable)
Requires Level 1A or Level 2 of UN R154
Requires Level 1A or Level 2 of UN R168 on real driving emissions (RDE) if applicable; PEMS defined per Annex 4 of R168
Requires compliance with UN Regulation No. [179] on brake particle emissions
Requires compliance with UN Regulation No. [180] on On-Board Monitoring (OBM) and Environmental Vehicle Passport (EVP)
Annex 9 uses definitions of UN Regulation No. 155 (cybersecurity)
Flex-fuel vehicle applications follow para 5.8 of UN R154
Certified/measured range per Appendix 3 to Annex C1 of R154.04; Type 4 ISC tests per Annex C3 of R154
Utility factor per Table A8.App5/1 of Appendix 5 to Annex B8 of R154

defined_terms.definition: A group of vehicles that fulfil the requirements for a vehicle type with regard to emissions per para 3.0.1 of UN R154.
The technically permissible maximum mass declared by the vehicle manufacturer.
The spaces in or external to an engine connected to the oil sump by internal or external ducts through which gases and vapour can escape.
Those components of a vehicle that control and/or limit exhaust and evaporative emissions.
Activities carried out on vehicles in circulation, systems, separate technical units or components to verify compliance with the durability requirements of this Regulation.
In the context of OBD in-use performance ratio, an engine coolant or equivalent temperature at start ≤ 35 °C and ≤ 7 °C above ambient.
Any product other than fuel stored on-board and provided to the exhaust after-treatment system upon request of the emission control system.
A portable emissions measurement system meeting the requirements of Annex 4 of UN R168.
An emission strategy active throughout the speed and load operating range unless an AES is activated.
An emission strategy that replaces or modifies a BES for a specific purpose in response to specific ambient or operating conditions, only while they exist.

Any element of design that makes a vehicle non-compliant when driven outside a regulatory test while appearing compliant when tested, or that manipulates sensor, consumption, range or battery durability data.
A strategy that makes a vehicle non-compliant when driven outside a regulatory test while appearing compliant when tested, or that manipulates sensor, consumption, range or battery durability data.

Inactivation or modification of the engine/motor, pollution control devices, propulsion system, traction battery, odometer, OBFCM, OBD or OBM, including software and data, resulting in non-compliance.
A rechargeable electrical energy storage system (REESS) installed in an electrified vehicle and used mainly for traction.
Energy supplied by the battery from the start of the certification test procedure until its break-off criterion is reached.
The range the certification range test would give at the present point in the vehicle lifetime with the originally installed battery.
The electric driving range determined during certification per Appendix 3 to Annex C1 of R154.04.
The electric range determined at the present point in the vehicle lifetime by the certification test procedure.
Measured or on-board UBE at a point in lifetime as a percentage of certified UBE.
Measured or on-board electric range at a point in lifetime as a percentage of certified range.
The minimum SOCE or SOCR durability performance at a point in lifetime constituting compliance.
A manufacturer-declared SOCE/SOCR value above the MPR that becomes the binding minimum durability performance.
An apparatus installed in the vehicle that estimates the state of certified range by an algorithm on vehicle system data.
An apparatus installed in the vehicle that estimates the state of certified energy by an algorithm on vehicle system data.
Estimates of SOCR / SOCE produced by the respective on-board monitor.
SOCR as measured range over certified range, and SOCE as measured UBE over certified UBE.
Use of traction batteries to cover external power demand, such as V2G, V2H and V2L.

defined_terms.term: Total discharge energy for non-traction purposes
defined_terms.definition: Total kWh discharged from the battery for non-traction purposes supporting a Category N vehicle use case, excluding cabin HVAC and uses already present in category M.
State of Certified Energy or State of Certified Range, as applicable.
Up to 160,000 km or 8 years, whichever comes first.
The period after main lifetime up to 200,000 km or 10 years, whichever comes first.
A manufacturer with fewer than 10,000 M1 or 22,000 N1 new EU registrations per year meeting group-related conditions, or as defined regionally by other contracting parties.

applicability_hints: Although titled for M1/N1 emissions, this version focuses on Type 3 (crankcase) and Type 6 (low temperature, positive ignition only) tests; Type 1/RDE etc. are referred to R154/R168 but compliance must be demonstrated in the application
Any ECU software or calibration affecting emission strategies (BES/AES) falls under manipulation-device scrutiny (Annex 7)
Anti-tampering/cybersecurity (Annex 9) covers engine/motor control, pollution control devices, traction battery, odometer, OBFCM, OBD and OBM including software and data
Battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles are in scope via battery durability ISC and SOCE/SOCR monitors even though they have no tailpipe emissions
Brake systems are relevant through brake emission ISC (para 9.5, Annex 12) and reference to R[179]
Reagent tanks/dosing (e.g. AdBlue/SCR) are pollution control/after-treatment components
Replacing make of a pollution control component does not automatically invalidate approval unless engine or pollution control functionality is affected (3.3.6)
N2 vehicles 3.5-5 t derived from N1 may be approved at manufacturer request
V2X/bidirectional charging use affects battery durability assessment (non-traction discharge energy for N vehicles)
